hannah: Hey infra team — customer ACME opened a ticket: their outbound firewall only allows a few IPs and our API calls are failing. They asked for a concrete egress IP list we can give them. Anyone have a short recommendation we can send?

samir: Short answer: hosted endpoints run behind region-scaled NAT pools. We can’t promise a single static IP for hosted traffic unless they use Dedicated/Private or we route via a paid static relay. Recommend hostname-based allowlisting or proxying.

maya: For customers:
- Recommended: allow by hostname/SNI (*.redwood.ai) so we never run into IP drift.
- Alternate: put our egress through their corporate proxy (we support HTTP CONNECT and mTLS).
- Last resort: provide current NAT ranges per region but include a warning about changes.

frank: Enterprise firewalls often refuse wildcard SNI. If they insist on IPs, we can provide the current stable blocks but must put expectations: IPs can change during autoscaling or infra migrations. Also we should offer a paid static-relay option with fixed IP pairs per region.

ops-bot: EGRESS-RANGES: latest snapshot uploaded to s3://redwood-static/egress/ranges-2026-02-28.csv and published at https://status.redwood.ai/egress-ranges.json

hannah: Can you list the most stable /24s we can give as "best-effort"? Need something the support agent can paste into the ticket.

samir: Telemetry shows US-WEST stable NAT pools covering ~88% traffic: 34.85.12.0/24, 34.85.13.0/24. EU-CENTRAL common: 35.201.200.0/21. Emphasize these are best-effort and add link to status page.

maya: Draft firewall snippet to send (add to KB):
```
# Option A - best-effort IP allowlist (subject to change)
allow tcp 443 to 34.85.12.0/24
allow tcp 443 to 34.85.13.0/24
allow tcp 443 to 35.201.200.0/21

# Option B - recommended: allow by hostname (SNI) or proxy CONNECT
allow tls to *.redwood.ai
allow proxy CONNECT to api.redwood.ai
```

frank: If they use a corporate proxy, ask them to configure it to forward TLS SNI intact or use CONNECT without intercept. If they must MITM, we’ll require client certs or an explicit proxy credential. We also accept a custom header for proxied setups: `X-Redwood-Proxy-Client: <team-id>`.

hannah: Also flag that some inline DPI can break streaming (chunked responses). If their proxy rewrites responses or terminates connections aggressively, streaming may fail.

maya: I'll update the KB: include the IP snapshot link, the recommended hostname option, guidance for proxies (CONNECT vs MITM), and a small checklist for onboarding. I'll add a note about subscribing to the egress feed for updates.

samir: Action item: eng-infra to draft a pricing + tech proposal for a static-relay product (fixed IP egress per region) we can offer to enterprise customers. I’ll drop a sketch into the sales playbook doc by COB.

frank: Ops suggestion: add an automated onboarding check that attempts both hostname and IP tests from the customer's network and returns a detailed diagnostic we can attach to support tickets.

hannah: Great — I'll reply to ACME recommending Option B (hostname/proxy) and include the best-effort IP list plus https://status.redwood.ai/egress-ranges.json. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
